dependency_notes: Story order follows dependency correctness only (per explicit run instruction), overriding Story Design Principle 4's 'simpler first' default -- several early stories (model, references, inference) are high-complexity precisely because everything downstream gates on them. Judgment calls made in this split, for the lead to override: (1) buffer.py's BufferedImage extension (carrying model identity + session-local reference identity) has no acceptance criterion of its own -- it is plumbing for AC-STATE-1/AC-STATE-2 -- so it is scoped into S6 (worker), which is where BufferedImage instances are constructed (worker.py:359-367), rather than spun out as its own story against the `buffer` module. (2) The new Tauri file-dialog command/plugin (desktop-shell) likewise has no AC of its own: AC-INPUT-1's verification explicitly targets the path-injection seam, not the native dialog, and AC-ACCESS-1 explicitly stubs the desktop bridge. It is scoped into S10 (desktop-ui) as thin, non-independently-tested glue -- the one deliberate exception to one-module-per-story outside the FR-A7 integration story. Split it into its own `desktop-shell` story if stricter module hygiene is wanted; it would then need a placeholder AC or an explicit AC-ownership exception. (3) Per architecture.md boundary rule 4, any wire-schema shape change is a mandatory three-language coordinated edit (protocol.py + the Rust json! builder + types.ts) done by ONE story, not split three ways -- S8 (ipc) therefore also touches src-tauri/src/commands_update_config.rs and src-tauri/ui/types.ts; this is architecture-sanctioned, not a one-module-ownership violation. (4) Several ACs describe behavior implemented across more than one module but carry no 'Spans modules:' line in acceptance-criteria.md (only AC-STATE-2 does) -- meaning Mode 1 judged them single-story-ownable. AC-STATE-1/3/4, AC-RECOVERY-1, AC-MODEL-5, AC-LOCAL-1, and AC-MODEL-6 were each assigned to the module whose code is most load-bearing for the AC's core mechanism; rebalance freely without touching acceptance-criteria.md. (5) AC-STATE-2's 'Spans modules:' line names desktop UI, IPC, backend state, worker, inference, metadata -- 'metadata' and 'backend state' both map to the `backend` module (architecture.md's module map has no separate `metadata` module), and 'desktop UI' maps to both S10 and S11 since both own `desktop-ui`. cross_cutting_acs[0].spanned_by is therefore [S5, S6, S7, S8, S10, S11], and S12 depends on that full set. (6) Seam source/destination endpoints describe runtime data-flow direction (producer -> consumer); the per-story `creates_seam` flag instead marks which story is accountable for freezing the contract's shape first in build order, and the two do not always point the same way -- e.g. GenerationRequest's shape is authored in inference/base.py by S5, even though S7 (backend) is the runtime producer of concrete request instances passed through S6 (worker) to S5's engines. (7) lighter_path is false on all twelve stories: every story's file targets include at least one non-markdown/JSON/YAML/TOML/txt file (.py, .rs, or .ts), so files_code is non-empty everywhere, which alone forces lighter_path=false under the AC-STORY-2 conjunction; S12 is additionally false by the mandatory is_integration_story exclusion.
mock_resolution_plan: No temporary mocks are introduced by this split. tests/mocks.py's MockInferenceEngine (exploration.json resistance point #1) is a permanent test fixture standing in for gated model weights, not an epic-temporary mock -- it is tracked as FIXTURE-05-001 on S5 and must be widened (not replaced) to keep implementing the extended InferenceEngine ABC. mocks-registry.json remains empty with all_resolved:true for this epic; Mode 2 introduces no entries requiring resolution.

blocking_conditions.source: Decider ruling 2026-09-18, findings F1/F2 from S3 Stage-1 review
blocking_conditions.condition: The fact 'model X's pipeline accepts reference inputs at dimensions D' MUST have exactly one derivation site, on the InferenceEngine instance in textbrush/inference/. S5 cannot close without (a) that accessor existing, (b) evidence from each editing pipeline -- not assumption -- of what it actually accepts, and (c) AC-MODEL-2/AC-MODEL-3 tests asserting the value at the model boundary. No slug-keyed dimension table. ModelSpec is NOT extended with a dimension field; S2 stays closed. S5 must also state which normalization shape each editing pipeline requires: (i) none, (ii) uniform scale to a fixed canvas with centered padding, or (iii) uniform scale to a bound / multiple-of-N without padding. Shapes (i) and (ii) are expressible through S3's target_size: tuple[int, int] | None. If any pipeline requires shape (iii), the S3 seam re-opens as a blocking finding against S5 -- it must NOT be worked around by rounding inside inference or by padding to the next multiple, both of which reintroduce the spec.md sec 6.2 model-boundary defect this condition exists to prevent.
blocking_conditions.rationale: spec.md sec 6.2 states what a pipeline accepts unchanged as a pipeline-runtime property, in the same breath as the duty to disable pipeline-internal resizing; only the code holding the pipeline can verify it. spec.md sec 5.5 explicitly decouples reference-input dimensions from the output presets. AC-MODEL-2/AC-MODEL-3 carry the 'disabled or handed a reference it accepts unchanged' disjunction that S5 must prove, so S5 must also be able to state it.
blocking_conditions.enforcement: Lead-enforced: read from stories.json and injected into each story's architect brief and reviewer brief, as was done for S2-BC-1. There is no automated gate.
blocking_conditions.on_failure: F1 re-opens as a blocking finding against S5. It must not be re-deferred, and must not be closed by S7 stubbing or defaulting the value.

stories.name: backend-config-lifecycle-and-metadata

stories.description: Give textbrush/backend.py a runtime model-swap path (it currently constructs self.engine once at __init__), construct the immutable per-request GenerationRequest snapshot, decode references exactly once at acknowledgement via S3's normalize() and hold them for the acknowledged configuration's lifetime, release them on change/abort/fatal-error/shutdown, and extend PNG/JPEG metadata writing to record the actual selected model without ever persisting reference identity.

stories.name: ipc-pause-gate-and-acknowledgement
stories.title: IPC Pause Gate and Configuration Acknowledgement
stories.description: Make textbrush/ipc/handler.py's handle_update_config (currently unconditional, handler.py:394-555) pause-gated, add the CONFIG_ACK message type (absent from protocol.py's MessageType today), acknowledge model/reference updates independently of their combined compatibility, refuse resume while incompatible with the required-model reason, serialize commands so a resume mid-update takes effect only after acknowledgement, and roll back to the last acknowledged configuration on any rejection or failure -- mirrored across the Python wire schema, the Rust IpcMessage payload, and types.ts per boundary rule 4.

Acknowledged-and-incompatible path: an individually valid update (readable reference, loadable model) is acknowledged even when the resulting combination can't generate; resume is refused with the reason while incompatible

Rejected-update rollback: unreadable/corrupt/unnormalizable reference, missing/gated/incomplete/unloadable model weights, or an off-paused attempt leaves the last acknowledged configuration active in both backend and (via the acknowledgement event) the UI
Command serialization: a resume arriving mid-update takes effect only after that update's acknowledgement

The three-language wire-schema mirror mandated by boundary rule 4: textbrush/ipc/protocol.py, src-tauri/src/commands_update_config.rs's json! builder, and src-tauri/ui/types.ts, made together in this story
excludes: The underlying quiescence signal itself (S6, worker) -- this story reports it, does not produce it

stories.description: Add reference-image selection to the desktop interface: a new Tauri file-dialog command/plugin (src-tauri/src) that yields a path list only, and TypeScript selection logic (src-tauri/ui) that consumes that path list for cardinality checks, per-file validation, preview construction with filename, individual removal/replacement, and compatibility/preset messaging -- keeping the dialog and the selection logic separable per spec.md sec 5.2's path-injection seam.

includes: New Tauri file-dialog plugin dependency and command (none exists in src-tauri today per exploration.json) whose sole responsibility is returning a path list

Selection logic operating on a supplied path list: accepts .png/.jpg/.jpeg case-insensitively, rejects more than four, displays previews with filenames, supports individual removal and replacement, preserves selection order internally
Per-file error surfacing for unsupported/unreadable/corrupt/resource-constrained files without starting generation

Rendering the BackendStateEvent acknowledgement/compatibility contract (recommended model naming/pre-highlighting per AC-MODEL-5, incompatibility reason/required-model per AC-STATE-4) -- the frontend never presents a configuration as active before acknowledgement
Disabling model/reference controls until the backend's settled signal, never on mere pause request
Upload control availability gated on an editing-capable model being active; FLUX.1 schnell cannot generate while references are active
excludes: The six editing-preset dimension table/compatibility rules themselves (S4, validation) -- this story only renders and forwards choices
Keyboard/ARIA/rendered-layout verification (S11)

stories.notes: Exploration.json resistance point #6 (zero prior UI precedent for file selection). The Tauri command is scoped here rather than as a separate desktop-shell story per top-level dependency_notes item 2 -- it has no independently verifiable AC of its own.

blocking_conditions.source: VQ-S2-005 (S2 verification), split from AC-MODEL-5 and bound by Decider ruling 2026-09-18
blocking_conditions.condition: AC-MODEL-5b: default-model resolution is invoked exactly ONCE per session, at launch, and never re-run in response to a reference-set change. resolve_model_selection is pure and cannot enforce this itself - only its callers can.

evidence_required.S8: A live IPC session driven across at least two reference-count changes crossing the cardinality boundary that would flip the resolver's answer, with a call counter on resolve_model_selection asserting exactly one invocation during initialization and zero thereafter, and the resolved model id unchanged throughout. ALSO owns the cross-cutting structural test (AST or equivalent, in the family of the mutation-tested model-leaf-boundary detector) asserting the function has exactly the enumerated set of production call sites and failing when a new caller appears - S8 is the first story to introduce a production caller.
evidence_required.S9: The same assertion at the CLI startup path. If the CLI is one-shot-per-process and cannot re-resolve by construction, S9 must state that explicitly and point at the single call site. An architectural argument is acceptable evidence; an unstated assumption is not.
evidence_required.S10: The user-facing half: adding or removing a reference never auto-switches the selected model, and an explicit user selection survives a reference-count change that would otherwise flip FLUX.1 to FLUX.2 or back.

blocking_conditions.enforcement: Lead-enforced: read from stories.json and injected into each story's architect brief and reviewer brief, as was done for S2-BC-1. There is no automated gate.
blocking_conditions.on_failure: AC-MODEL-5b re-opens as a blocking finding against the story that closed without it. It must not be re-deferred.

stories.name: desktop-accessibility-harness
stories.title: Desktop Accessibility Verification Harness
stories.description: Adopt a headless-browser test harness (none exists today; the project's UI tests run via node --test over compiled *.test.js with jsdom, not a real renderer) with the desktop bridge stubbed, and use it to verify keyboard reachability, accessible labels, text-form error presentation, and the four-preview layout at supported window sizes for the controls S10 built -- static source inspection/pattern-matching does not satisfy this requirement.

includes: New headless-browser test harness adoption (e.g. Playwright) as real scope, per exploration.json's explicit call-out, with the desktop/Tauri bridge stubbed so no backend or native dialog is required
Keyboard operability and programmatic labels for selecting/previewing/replacing/removing reference files, asserted against the rendered interface
Errors available as text, not relying on color alone; preview accessible names derived from filename+position without claiming inferred image content
Four-preview layout at supported desktop window sizes: no control loses keyboard/pointer reachability, no preview is clipped by overflow
Existing focus/theme/font-size/disabled-state conventions preserved for the new controls
excludes: Building the controls themselves (S10) -- this story verifies what S10 already implemented and may return small accessibility fixes to S10's files where a gap is found

stories.notes: Exploration.json resistance point #8 and the aria_gap testing note: ARIA attributes already exist in source (main.ts:926,959-988; config_controls.ts:372) but no test asserts them today. Deliberately sequenced after S10 (cannot verify keyboard reachability of controls that do not yet exist) and shares owning_module 'desktop-ui' with S10 -- see top-level dependency_notes item 2's sibling reasoning; flagged as a judgment call in the top-level notes rather than repeated per-story.

stories.name: cross-cutting-config-change-integration
stories.title: Cross-Cutting Configuration-Change Integration Verification
stories.description: Verify, across real (already-implemented) desktop UI, IPC, backend, worker, inference, and metadata code -- no mocked producers -- the whole-flow guarantee that every displayed or persisted result's provenance is correct across arbitrary pause/update/resume/generate/navigate/delete sequences, per architecture.md's Order-Sensitive Composition section and AC-STATE-2.

includes: End-to-end sequences of pause, valid configuration update, resume, generation completion, navigation, and deletion exercised against the real S5/S6/S7/S8/S10/S11 implementations
Assertion that every displayed result's session record retains the prompt, model, seed, and dimensions from the single snapshot that generated it
Assertion that no reference identity is persisted in session records beyond what AC-META-1 already permits in output files

Adversarial falsification pass over interleavings named in architecture.md's Order-Sensitive Composition section (stale-result visibility, control-enablement window, snapshot attribution, partial reference application, decode-lifetime, resume-during-update)
excludes: Any new production behavior -- this story is verification-only against the assembled whole; a real gap found here is fixed in the owning story's files, not re-implemented here

stories.notes: FR-A7 integration story. Depends on the union of AC-STATE-2's spanned_by set: S5, S6, S7, S8, S10, S11 (translated from architecture.md's 'desktop UI, IPC, backend state, worker, inference, metadata' -- see top-level dependency_notes item 5). Runs last in story_order for exactly this reason. Omits owning_module by design (it spans modules rather than owning one) and is exempt from the one-module-per-story rule per Module Ownership principle 5's explicit FR-A7 carve-out.

stories.name: user-documentation
stories.title: Desktop and CLI Documentation for Reference Editing
stories.description: Document the reference-editing workflow for desktop and CLI users per spec.md section 16, and write the release notes describing this as an additive editing workflow that requires FLUX.2 for two to four references.

includes: Capability differences among FLUX.1 schnell, FLUX.1 Kontext [dev] and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B
Supported reference counts and file formats, and the six editing output presets
Worked examples for one-reference Kontext and multi-reference FLUX.2 usage, desktop and CLI
Local model storage, gated-license, credential, hardware and memory expectations
That prompt wording controls identity and reference use, with no guaranteed identity fidelity
Local-only processing and the metadata privacy policy
First-release limitations and the later face-aware-cropping direction
Release notes per spec.md section 16
excludes: docs/configuration.md's [editing]/[model].selected_id reference, folded into S1 where the change originated
Any behavioral code change

stories.notes: Added mid-epic. The original 12-story split left spec.md section 16 (Release and Documentation Requirements) unowned, and section 16 carried no acceptance criterion, so the end-of-epic AC-closure gate would not have caught the omission either. Surfaced by the S1 round-2 review noticing docs/configuration.md drift. Placed last so it documents the shipped behavior.
